children.title: Dissipation Bounds in Predictive Information Engines

detail.title: Dissipation Bounds in Predictive Information Engines
detail.summary: This provisional analysis explores how autonomous information engines use internal memory states to leverage temporal correlations. Evidence indicates that nonreciprocal coupling modulates information flow, and engines require multiple memory states to facilitate self-correction in the presence of environmental fluctuations. Thermodynamic costs of memory maintenance remain tightly linked to the ability of the engine to synchronize with external dynamics.
detail.reason: Synthesis of collected evidence to address the project question regarding predictive state dissipation modulation.
